newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Novus sees 30 mln extra boe from projects.
newsitem.headline: Novus sees 30 mln extra boe from projects.

text.p: Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Thursday that three new developments were likely to contribute about 30 million barrels of oil equivalent to its booked reserves, which is equal to over three years production at current rate.
Novus chairman John Fitzgerald told the annual general meeting that Novus had "already very comfortably replaced its project full year production for 1997."
Net production in 1996 was 23,657 barrels of oil equivalent per day.

New projects include the Kakap production sharing contract area offshore Indonesia, which includes output from the Nelayan field, and six new areas in the Carvarvon Basin, offshore Western and an addititonal 30 percent share in Bukha oilfield in Oman.
Fitzgerald said Novus would also commence production from another two offshore oilfields in the Kakap production sharing contract area offshore Indonesia.
This includes output from the Nelayan field, which Fitzgerald said commenced production earlier this week at a daily rate of 4,700 barrels of oil.

Fitzgerald also told shareholders there were promising developments occuring another two exploration wells in the Novus portfolio, the Singha-1 well in Sumatra, Indonesia, and the Miriwah-1 well in Pakistan.
Indications from the main reservoir target of Singha-1 was consistent with a potentially commercial discovery.
"At this stage, we have little idea of its size, but it is located in an area surroudned by existing fields and infrastructure," Fitzgerald said.
The Miriwah-1 well, located in the Sulaiman fold belt of Pakistan, is currently being tested, he said.

"Howver, in both cases we should not at this stage bank either of these wells as new field discoveries as a fuller programme of evaluation and testing will be required to determine the commercial significance of both wells," Fitzgerald said.
Novus was budgeting about US$35 million on exploration in 1997, enabling it to participate in at least 20 exploration wells during the year.
